text:
Maria: PagerBot alert for eu-west-2 GPU pool — ~45% of dedicated GPU nodes reported NotReady, workload throttling visible. Not sure if autoscaler kicked.
PagerBot: INCIDENT ALERT: eu-west-2-gpu-pool degraded. Severity: P1. Affected: dedicated/private GPU tiers. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eu2-gpu
Jon: Ack, I'm taking ownership. Paging oncall: @Akshay — can you join? :eyes:
Akshay: Acked. Looking at node logs now. Seeing repeated `nv_peer_mem` and `nvidia` kernel oops. Autoscaler metrics show pending but no scale-up events in the last 10m.
Lisa: On one repro node I rolled driver 535 -> 530 and kernel oops stopped. Reboot + driver rollback restored GPU devices. Suggest we try a staged rollback on a small subset.
Maria: Good call. If rollback succeeds, we still need traffic handling. eu-central has spare capacity but higher latency — can we divert traffic gradually? We should avoid hard cutovers.
Akshay: Proposing routing plan:
```
# Incremental shift using router CLI
router shift --from eu-west-2 --to eu-central-1 --percent 25 --duration 5m
wait 5m
router shift --percent 50
wait 10m
router shift --percent 100
```
Start canary at +2m. I'll initiate the 25% canary now.
Jon: Also: autoscaler didn't scale due to `scaleDownDisabled` flag set on some nodes after previous maintenance. We should patch the check to ignore transient NotReady caused by driver panic for 5m window.
Maria: Agreed. Action items: (1) staged driver rollback and node reboot; (2) start routing canary to eu-central; (3) temp autoscaler tweak and add defensive logging to runbook.
sre-rotation-bot: Oncall handoff scheduled: Akshay -> Jon at 09:00 UTC. Current incident will be carried by oncall until resolved.
Akshay: Canary 25% in flight. Observing tail latency +160ms for affected endpoints, error rate unchanged. Rolling rollback to next 10 nodes.
Lisa: Rolling image tag to `nvidia-driver:530-pin` on pool nodes now. Command used:
```
kubectl -n infra set image ds/gpu-driver gpu-driver=image:530-pin --record
```
Jon: Slight tweak to pager policy proposal: for driver-related kernel oops, don't escalate to paging if overall capacity >60% and error rate <1% for 10m. Instead send high-urgency ops channel alert. We should discuss RFC after incident.
Maria: I've started a minimal incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2025-eu2-gpu-deg. Adding rollback timeline and postmortem checklist.
PagerBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: rollback progressing, node count returning to Ready. Current capacity estimate: 78%.
Akshay: Rolling to remaining nodes. Autoscaler now shows scale events are allowed; no pending pods after reboots.
PagerBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: eu-west-2 GPU pool recovered to 98% capacity after driver rollback + controlled reboots. Monitoring for 30m. Incident closed at 1754001534.
Jon: Final notes before handoff: implement pager tweak doc, add a non-paging transient-flap channel, add driver-version gating to autoscaler heuristics, and run a dry-run of the routing shift playbook. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Maria: I'll own the postmortem and the follow-ups. Adding owners to the runbook PR now.
